findings.principle: Loss aversion (prospect theory) — and its modern moderators
findings.what: Kahneman & Tversky (1979) proposed that losses are weighted more than equal gains; Tversky & Kahneman (1992) estimated the loss-aversion coefficient at λ ≈ 2.25 from a small sample of hypothetical choices. Gal & Rucker (2018, J. Consumer Psychology 28:497–516) argued the '2:1 universal law' is not supported and that the asymmetry depends on context, stakes and population. Mrkva, Johnson, Gächter & Herrmann (2020, JCP 30:407–428) answered with five samples (N total = 17,720): loss aversion is real at every knowledge level but shrinks with domain knowledge/experience; a 2024 meta-analysis and a JDM paper report that it does not materialize for small stakes. Net: robust for meaningful stakes (₪279–₪749 is meaningful for a gift), weaker for trivial amounts and for experienced buyers.
findings.source: Tversky & Kahneman 1992, J. Risk & Uncertainty — https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF00122574 ; Gal & Rucker 2018 — https://myscp.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/jcpy.1047 ; Mrkva et al. 2020 — https://myscp.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/jcpy.1156
findings.honestApplication: The gift buyer's salient loss is not the ₪299 — it is 'I gave the wrong thing to someone I love'. Every honest lever here reduces that potential loss rather than manufacturing a new one. (1) The site already carries three loss-reducers (insured shipping, 12-month body warranty, 30-day return) in the ASSURANCE line in components/ProductView.tsx; keep them exactly where they are (under the button, where the loss is imagined). (2) Do NOT use loss framing that implies a deadline or dwindling stock — that would violate the store's rules and, per Gal & Rucker, is the least reliable part of the effect anyway. (3) The one loss the buyer can be truthfully warned about is engraving the wrong text: the mustChoose gate (line 57) already blocks a default blessing from being burned. Say why, in one line near the chooser: 'הנוסח נצרב לפי ההזמנה — לכן בוחרים כאן' (the text is burned per order — so you choose here). That is loss-aware copy with a real referent. (4) The free-shipping threshold (₪550, lib/policy.ts) and the cart progress bar are a real, verifiable threshold; Lewis, Singh & Fay 2006 (Marketing Science 25:51–64) found threshold free shipping effective with actual retailer data. Keep it; never lower the number below what the server enforces.

findings.principle: Risk reversal — return policy generosity and its long-run effect
findings.what: Bower & Maxham (2012, Journal of Marketing 76:110–124) ran field studies with two leading online retailers over 49 months combining surveys and actual spending data. Customers who received free return shipping increased their purchases over the following two years by between 58% and 357%; customers who had to pay return shipping decreased subsequent purchases by between 74% and 100%. Fairness perceptions did not reverse either effect. Suwelack, Hogreve & Hoyer (2011, Journal of Retailing 87:462–478) showed in two experiments that money-back guarantees raise purchase intention and willingness to pay a premium, and that for experience goods the guarantee should have clearer (stricter) conditions to remain believable.
findings.source: Bower & Maxham 2012 — https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/abs/10.1509/jm.10.0419 (figures via UVA release: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2012/10/121009101344.htm) ; Suwelack et al. 2011 — https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0022435911000820
findings.honestApplication: There is a gap between what the storefront says and what the terms say. ProductView.tsx / Closing.tsx / the header ticker say 'החזרה תוך 30 יום'; lib/legal.ts lines 95–99 add that on a non-defect return the company may charge up to 5% or ₪100 and the customer bears return shipping. That is legal, but Bower & Maxham says fee returns are the single most damaging policy for repeat buying, and a gift buyer who discovers the fee only in the terms will feel tricked. Two honest paths: (a) Owner decides returns are genuinely free (waive the 5% fee, cover return courier for the first return) — then change lib/legal.ts and add one derivable line under the button: 'לא מתאים? החזרה תוך 30 יום, המשלוח חזרה עלינו'. (b) Owner keeps the fee — then say the condition plainly near the promise ('החזרה תוך 30 יום · דמי משלוח חזרה על הלקוח'), because a guarantee with hidden conditions is the kind Suwelack found to be less believable. Either way, surface the store's genuinely unusual advantage that lib/faq.ts already states: because the texts come from a closed list, the item is NOT a custom-made good and the statutory 14-day cancellation right fully applies — most engraved-jewellery competitors cannot say that. Put that sentence in the 'איך אפשר לדעת' box, not only in the FAQ.

findings.principle: Choice overload (the jam study) — what the evidence actually shows
findings.what: Iyengar & Lepper (2000) reported that a tasting booth with 24 jams drew 60% of passers-by vs 40% for 6 jams, but 30% of the 6-jam visitors bought vs 3% of the 24-jam visitors. Scheibehenne, Greifeneder & Todd (2010, JCR 37:409) meta-analysed 63 conditions from 50 experiments (N = 5,036) and found 'a mean effect size of virtually zero but considerable variance between studies', a slight publication bias toward positive results, and no sufficient conditions; a necessary precondition they flag is lack of prior preference (people with clear preferences prefer larger sets — Chernev 2003). Chernev, Böckenholt & Goodman (2015, JCP 25:333–358), with 99 observations (N = 7,202), found that once four moderators are included the effect is significant: choice overload appears when choice-set complexity is high, the decision task is difficult, preference uncertainty is high (no articulated ideal point / low expertise), and the buyer has an effort-minimising goal.
findings.source: Scheibehenne et al. 2010 — https://scheibehenne.com/ScheibehenneGreifenederTodd2010.pdf ; Chernev et al. 2015 — https://chernev.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/02/ChoiceOverload_JCP_2015.pdf ; Iyengar & Lepper 2000 — https://faculty.washington.edu/jdb/345/345%20Articles/Iyengar%20&%20Lepper%20(2000).pdf
findings.honestApplication: The number of options at mikra.shop (15 designs, 5 blessings, 2–3 per design) is not the problem; the moderator that bites is preference uncertainty, and a gift buyer has it by definition (they are choosing for someone else). The honest remedy is to give them an articulated ideal point, not to cut the catalogue. Concretely: (1) Keep the 'forWhom' line on every blessing card (ProductView.tsx line 513) — it is exactly the 'ideal point' Chernev describes. (2) Make recipient/occasion the primary entry, not material: the eight guides in lib/guides.data.ts (mother, enlistment, reserves, big trip, new business…) already do this; promote them into the category pages as a filter row ('למי: אמא · חייל · עסק חדש · תינוק') so the buyer arrives at 2–3 candidates with a reason. (3) In lib/faq.ts the 'איך בוחרים בין 3 הנוסחים' answer already maps blessing → recipient; add the same mapping one line under the chooser heading so it is read before the decision, not after. (4) Do not add a sixth blessing or extra finishes 'for variety' without a recipient-based reason. What is NOT allowed and NOT needed: 'most popular', 'best seller' or 'X people chose' labels — the store has no data for them and the research shows a clear recommendation rule works without popularity claims.

findings.principle: Default effects (endorsement, endowment, ease)
findings.what: Jachimowicz, Duncan, Weber & Johnson (2019, Behavioural Public Policy 3:159–186) meta-analysed 58 datasets from 55 studies (N = 73,675). Defaults had a medium effect, Cohen's d = 0.68 (95% CI 0.53–0.83), about a 27.24-percentage-point difference in binary choices — larger than social-norm or framing nudges — but with I² = 98.21% heterogeneity, several null and two negative studies. Two mechanisms were significant: endorsement (the default reads as the choice architect's recommendation, b = 0.32) and endowment/status quo (b = 0.31); 'ease' was not (b = −0.05). Defaults were far stronger in consumer domains (b = 0.89) than environmental ones (b = −0.60), plausibly because consumer preferences are weaker. The authors warn to test each application rather than assume it works.
findings.source: Jachimowicz et al. 2019 — https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/behavioural-public-policy/article/when-and-why-defaults-influence-decisions-a-metaanalysis-of-default-effects/67AF6972CFB52698A60B6BD94B70C2C0
findings.honestApplication: Because a default is read as an endorsement, the site's current refusal to silently default the blessing (picked flag, ProductView.tsx line 55) is correct for an irreversible engraving and must stay. Where defaults are honest: (1) Shipping method defaults to home delivery with pickup shown as an equal card (CheckoutForm.tsx) — good. (2) Gift box defaults OFF (lib/extras.ts) — keep it off; pre-ticking a paid add-on is the dark-pattern version and the Israeli consumer regulator treats it as such. (3) Marketing consent unticked and separate (Section 30A) — keep. The one place to USE the endorsement mechanism honestly is to replace a silent default with a labelled recommendation derived from content: on a product whose blessings include Eshet Chayil, when the buyer arrived from the 'gift for mother' guide (query param or referrer), pre-highlight — not pre-select — that card with the caption 'הנוסח שנכתב לאם' (the text written for a mother). The reason is verifiable (Proverbs 31 is about a woman), so it is an endorsement with a source, not an invented popularity default. Still require the click.

findings.principle: Anchoring
findings.what: Tversky & Kahneman (1974) spun a rigged wheel to 10 or 65 before asking the share of African UN members; mean estimates were 25% vs 45%. Ariely, Loewenstein & Prelec (2003, QJE 118:73–105) had 55 MBA students write the last two digits of their social-security number before bidding: subjects with above-median numbers stated values 57%–107% higher; top-quintile subjects bid $56 on average for a cordless keyboard vs $16 for bottom-quintile, yet relative ordering (keyboard > trackball) was stable for ~95%. Many Labs 1 (Klein et al. 2014, 36 samples, N = 6,344) replicated four anchoring items in 100% of samples with replication effect sizes larger than the original (d ≈ 1.27 for NYC distance to d ≈ 2.60 for babies born). Anchoring is among the most reliably replicated effects in the literature.
findings.source: Ariely et al. 2003 — https://www.cmu.edu/dietrich/sds/docs/loewenstein/CoherentArbit.pdf ; Klein et al. 2014 Many Labs — https://stanford.edu/~knutson/jdm/klein14.pdf ; Tversky & Kahneman 1974 Science 185:1124
findings.honestApplication: Fake 'was' prices are the dishonest anchor and are already off (AUTO_DISCOUNT = false, compareAt never populated in lib/catalog.ts — keep the field empty unless a price was actually charged for 21 consecutive days, as lib/promo.ts notes). Honest anchors that already exist and can be ordered deliberately: (1) The 'מאיפה מתחילים' row (components/home/Bestsellers.tsx) shows the ₪749 Toldot first, which makes ₪279–₪349 read as moderate; that is a real price in the real catalogue, so it is legitimate — keep the featured flagship first. (2) The installment line '5 תשלומים של כ־₪150' re-anchors on a monthly figure that is derived by perInstallment(); keep it directly under the price. (3) The word count is a derivable anchor: '204 מילים' on the Eshet Chayil card gives scale to a ₪279 price without any claim; the product FAQ could add 'המחיר זהה לכל נוסח' (already there) so the buyer does not anchor on length = price. (4) On category pages, sort by price ascending by default only if you want ₪279 to be the anchor; sorting flagship-first anchors high. Decide once and derive it, do not hand-order. Not allowed: 'שווי ₪1,200', 'מחיר השקה', or any reference price with no charged history.

findings.principle: Decision fatigue / ego depletion — largely failed to replicate; what remains is difficulty-driven deferral
findings.what: The 'depletion' claim behind decision fatigue did not survive preregistered tests: Hagger et al. (2016, Perspectives on Psychological Science) ran the ego-depletion paradigm in 23 labs with >2,000 participants and found an overall effect close to zero; Vohs et al. (2021, Psychological Science, 36 labs, N = 3,531) found d = 0.06, with the data 4.4 times more likely under the null. The 'hungry judges' study (Danziger, Levav & Avnaim-Pesso 2011, PNAS: favorable parole rulings fall from ~65% to ~0% before a break) was challenged by Weinshall-Margel & Shapard (2011, PNAS) — case order was not random (unrepresented prisoners went last) — and by Glöckner (2016, JDM), whose simulation showed a rational judge who avoids starting long (favorable, 7.37 min vs 5.21 min) cases before a break produces the same curve. What does replicate is choice deferral when the task is hard or options are close: Dhar (1997, JCR 24:215–231, seven studies) showed deferral rises when alternatives are similar in attractiveness; Novemsky et al. (2007) showed 17% deferred a phone choice in an easy font vs 41% in a hard font.
findings.source: Vohs et al. 2021 — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12422598/ ; Hagger et al. 2016 — https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/1745691616652873 ; Glöckner 2016 — https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/judgment-and-decision-making/article/irrational-hungry-judge-effect-revisited-simulations-reveal-that-the-magnitude-of-the-effect-is-overestimated/61CE825D4DC137675BB9CAD04571AE58 ; Dhar 1997 — https://academic.oup.com/jcr/article-abstract/24/2/215/1794929
findings.honestApplication: Do not build anything on 'they are tired, so push them'. Build on 'a close call gets postponed'. The purchase path currently asks eight decisions: blessing, finish, quantity, gift box (asked twice — product page and CartDrawer), shipping method, ship-to-recipient, terms, marketing. Honest reductions: (1) Ask gift box once — keep the product-page toggle, make the cart one a passive summary line with an 'עריכה' link rather than a second switch. (2) Make the blessing choice a non-close call: the cards already differ by recipient; add the one-line recipient mapping above the grid so two of three options become obviously 'not for her' (Dhar: deferral falls as the attractiveness gap grows). (3) Quantity stepper on the product page is noise for a gift of one item; keep it but default 1 and visually secondary (already). (4) The comment in ProductView.tsx notes the buy button sits at 1,176 px on mobile vs 790 at the category leader — that is the real 'fatigue': distance, not depletion. The sticky bar is the fix and it is flagged as unverified on a real phone in CLAUDE.md; verifying it is worth more than any persuasion copy. Do not add exit-intent popups or 'still deciding?' nudges — they add decisions.

findings.principle: Anticipated regret and regret aversion in a gift purchase
findings.what: Simonson (1992, JCR 19:105–118) tested exactly this scenario: 218 undergraduates were told to buy a wedding gift for a close relative from a store catalogue with monthly sales. Merely asking them first to anticipate which error they would regret more raised the share who bought now (July) instead of waiting for a possibly better August sale from 54% (control) to 63% (regret condition), and raised the share choosing the higher-priced well-known brand over a cheaper lesser-known one from 50% to 67%. Waiting and missing a deal was expected to feel like the more self-blaming error; choosing the safe, conventional option was expected to carry less regret. Zeelenberg (1999, J. Behavioral Decision Making 12:93–106) generalised: anticipated regret pushes toward choices that are safer and whose outcomes will be less exposed to comparison. Buyers of gifts face two-sided regret: wrong gift vs missed date.
findings.source: Simonson 1992 — http://web.mit.edu/curhan/www/docs/Articles/biases/19_J_Consumer_Research_105_(Simonson).pdf ; Zeelenberg 1999 — https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/(SICI)1099-0771(199906)12:2%3C93::AID-BDM311%3E3.0.CO;2-S
findings.honestApplication: The honest counterpart to a countdown timer is a computed date. components/DeliveryEstimate.tsx already turns '2–4 business days' into 'מגיע אליכם 18–22 בספטמבר' from real policy numbers. Extend it with an optional, buyer-entered occasion: a small 'מתי צריך את זה?' date field on the product page (or checkout) that returns a derived answer — 'הזמנה עד יום ה׳ מגיעה לפני ה־25' — or, when the date is too close, says so and offers pickup in Modi'in (₪0, same day by arrangement). Every number in that sentence comes from POLICY.deliveryMinDays/MaxDays and the buyer's own input; nothing is invented, and it addresses the 'missed the date' regret Simonson measured. Second, make the 'wrong gift' regret reversible and say it in gift terms: lib/faq.ts already states the blessing can be changed before shipping and returns are 30 days — put a one-liner beside the recipient checkbox in CheckoutForm.tsx: 'אם הנוסח לא מתאים לה, אפשר להחליף עד המשלוח בוואטסאפ'. Third, Simonson's 'safe conventional option' is, for this store, the source itself (Proverbs 31 for a mother, Psalm 121 for a soldier) — lean on the source's conventionality, not on brand fame the store does not have. Not allowed: 'הזמינו היום כי המלאי אוזל', fake order counters, or generic urgency.

findings.principle: Giver–receiver asymmetries (what gift recipients actually value)
findings.what: Gino & Flynn (2011, J. Experimental Social Psychology 47:915–922; five experiments incl. wedding-registry and Amazon-wishlist studies) found recipients appreciate gifts they explicitly requested more than unrequested ones, while givers wrongly assume both are equally appreciated and that unrequested gifts signal more thoughtfulness. Flynn & Adams (2009, JESP 45:404–409) found givers expect appreciation to rise with price, but recipients report no link between price and appreciation. Baskin, Wakslak, Trope & Novemsky (2014, JCR 41:169–182) showed givers construe gifts abstractly and overweight desirability, whereas receivers weight feasibility (how easy it is to actually use). Together: the hesitant giver overrates 'impressive' and underrates 'usable and wanted'.
findings.source: Gino & Flynn 2011 — https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0022103111000801 ; Flynn & Adams 2009 — https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0022103108002175 ; Baskin et al. 2014 — https://academic.oup.com/jcr/article-abstract/41/1/169/1810280
findings.honestApplication: (1) Feasibility over desirability in gift copy: the catalogue already holds the usable facts — adjustable 42+5 cm chain, extension chain on bracelets, low profile, 'can be worn under a shirt', sealed water-resistant window, care rules. Surface two of them in the product 'story' or in a short 'ביום-יום' line under the assurance row, instead of adding more grandeur. (2) Explicitness: offer a legitimate 'let her choose' path. Because engraving happens per order (mustChoose gate exists for this reason), the store can sell a design with the blessing left open and send the recipient a WhatsApp link to pick the text before burning; that is Gino & Flynn's 'requested gift' without a registry. This is an operations decision (order meta + a hold state in WooCommerce), not a copy change — flag to the owner. (3) Price: do not push the ₪749 flagship as 'the better gift'; Flynn & Adams says the recipient will not feel the difference. Let the guides recommend by recipient, and let the ₪279–₪349 tier be presented without apology. (4) The included blessing card (name, sources, full text) is the feasibility item that makes the gift usable at the moment of giving — it is already in the box; mention it beside the gift-box toggle, not only in the spec accordion.

findings.principle: Cognitive (processing) fluency
findings.what: Song & Schwarz (2008, Psychological Science 19:986–988) gave identical exercise instructions in Arial vs a hard-to-read script font: readers estimated 8.2 minutes vs 15.1 minutes and were less willing to adopt the routine; the same held for a sushi recipe (Mistral vs Arial). Novemsky, Dhar, Schwarz & Simonson (2007, JMR 44:347–356) presented two cordless phones in easy vs hard fonts: 17% deferred choice with the easy font vs 41% with the hard one, and telling people 'this may be hard to read because of the font' dropped deferral back to 16%. Reber & Schwarz (1999) showed fluently presented statements are judged more likely true. The mechanism is misattribution: felt difficulty of reading is read as difficulty of the decision, the task, or doubt about the claim.
findings.source: Song & Schwarz 2008 — https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1111/j.1467-9280.2008.02189.x (figures via Song & Schwarz, The Psychologist 2010: https://dornsife.usc.edu/norbert-schwarz/wp-content/uploads/sites/231/2023/12/10_TP_Song__Schwarz_Easy.pdf) ; Novemsky et al. 2007 JMR 44:347–356
findings.honestApplication: This store sells text, so disfluency is a product feature on the chip and a conversion cost everywhere else. (1) Product names carry niqqud (תּוֹלְדוֹת) — keep it in the h1 and cards, but never in buttons, the sticky bar, cart lines or prices; the `plain` field in lib/blessings.ts exists for this and CartDrawer already uses it. (2) Inconsistent numbers are disfluency that reads as doubt: CLAUDE.md records that the site publishes three mutually inconsistent letter-height figures (9 µm on the site, 15 in the engraving script, and no measurement behind either). Reber & Schwarz's fluency–truth link means the fix is to resolve the number, not to explain it; until measured, publish one figure with 'כ־' as the site already does. (3) The 'איך אפשר לדעת' box and the assurance line are one-sentence items — keep that register; resist adding icon grids. (4) The Hero's 'עד 4,937 תווים' is derived from the text (LONGEST_BLESSING_CHARS) — good; keep every number derived so it cannot drift. (5) Novemsky's attribution finding suggests one honest micro-copy where the buyer must read unpointed biblical Hebrew: label the full-text page 'הנוסח כפי שהוא נצרב, עם טעמים' so difficulty is attributed to the text, not to the decision.

findings.principle: Endowment effect and psychological ownership from touch or imagery
findings.what: Kahneman, Knetsch & Thaler (1990, JPE 98:1325–1348) randomly gave half of a class Cornell mugs: median sellers asked $5.25, median buyers offered $2.75, and only 4, 1, 2 and 2 trades occurred across sessions where 11 were predicted. Plott & Zeiler (2005, AER 95:530–545) showed the WTA–WTP gap for mugs can be 'turned on and off' by procedures that remove subject misconceptions, but their claim is contested and a 2015 replication attempt failed to reproduce their null. Peck & Shu (2009, JCR 36:434–447, four studies) found merely touching an object raises perceived ownership and willingness to pay, and that for non-owners 'imagery encouraging touch' or imagining ownership produces the same rise — they explicitly note online retailers can use no-touch + ownership imagery. Brasel & Gips (2014, JCP 24:226–233, two lab studies) found touchscreen interaction increases psychological ownership and magnifies the endowment effect, more so for products where haptics matter and on a device the user owns.
findings.source: KKT 1990 — https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/doi/abs/10.1086/261737 (figures via Columbia lecture notes https://www.columbia.edu/~md3405/BE_Ref_1_17.pdf) ; Plott & Zeiler 2005 — https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257%2F0002828054201387 ; Peck & Shu 2009 — https://academic.oup.com/jcr/article-abstract/36/3/434/2900262 ; Brasel & Gips 2014 — https://myscp.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1016/j.jcps.2013.10.003
findings.honestApplication: Ownership imagery is honest as long as the image is of the real product and the claim is derivable. (1) The NanoLoupe on the 'הברכה על השבב' view is a touch/drag interaction on the buyer's own phone — exactly Brasel & Gips's strongest case; make it the second thumbnail on mobile rather than last, and let the drag reveal the actual chosen text (it already renders the selected blessing). (2) The 'על הדגם' worn view exists for most products; two models (chishuk, tzel-knafayim) have none — shoot them, because for a gift the ownership image is the recipient wearing it. (3) Ownership copy without invented claims: 'הנוסח שבחרתם' (the text you chose) after the pick, the blessing colour following through cart → checkout → success (already implemented) — this is the buyer's choice becoming 'theirs' before payment. (4) Pickup in Modi'in is the only real touch opportunity before paying; lib/policy.ts already treats it as an equal option — keep it prominent for local buyers. Not allowed: 'imagine her tears', staged testimonials, or fabricated unboxing 'reviews'. Note the endowment literature's caveat: the effect is procedure-sensitive, so treat this as a modest, cheap lever, not a headline strategy.

findings.principle: Commitment and consistency (foot-in-the-door)
findings.what: Freedman & Fraser (1966, JPSP 4:195–202): people who first agreed to a small request (answer a short survey) complied 52.8% with a large intrusive one vs 22.2% for cold contacts; in the second experiment a small 'safe driver' sign raised acceptance of a large ugly 'Drive Carefully' billboard even when the first request was on a different issue. Beaman et al. (1983, PSPB 9:181–196) meta-analysed 120 experimental groups and concluded the phenomenon is replicable but weak, with nearly half of studies showing no effect or a reversal; Burger (1999, PSPR 3:303–325) reviewed >100 studies and identified several processes (self-perception, consistency, reactance) that can also cancel it. Cialdini's 'consistency' principle rests on this literature — real but small and easily broken by perceived manipulation.
findings.source: Freedman & Fraser 1966 — https://psycnet.apa.org/record/1966-10825-001 ; Beaman et al. 1983 — https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/abs/10.1177/0146167283092002 ; Burger 1999 — https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1207/s15327957pspr0304_2
findings.honestApplication: Given the weak, fragile effect, use only the commitments the buyer wants to make anyway. (1) The blessing choice is the meaningful commitment; the flow already asks for it before the button and the sticky bar scrolls back to it — that ordering is right. Reading the full text ('לקריאת הנוסח המלא') is a second natural micro-commitment; keep the link adjacent to the chooser. (2) The club code (MIKRA20 for the first order, via the popup/footer) is a small ask that returns a real benefit — that is honest foot-in-the-door; do not follow it with 'you already started, finish now' emails (there is no outbound email anyway, per CLAUDE.md). (3) Cart persistence in localStorage keeps the commitment across sessions — already there. (4) Avoid forced micro-yeses ('Do you want to give her a blessing? Yes/No') — Burger's review shows manufactured commitments trigger reactance. Nothing here needs invented numbers; the lever is sequencing, and the expected lift is small.

findings.principle: Reciprocity
findings.what: Regan (1971, JESP 7:627–639): participants who received an unsolicited Coke from a confederate bought twice as many raffle tickets (M = 2.0 vs 0.9), and the effect was driven by felt obligation rather than liking. Strohmetz, Rind, Fisher & Lynn (2002, J. Applied Social Psychology 32:300–309): a piece of candy with the bill raised tips from 15.06% to 17.84% of the bill in Experiment 1; in Experiment 2 one candy raised tips ~3.3%, two candies ~14.1%, and the personal manner of giving mattered. Kunz & Woolcott (1976, Social Science Research 5:269–278) sent 578 Christmas cards to strangers and 20% replied; Meier's 2015 replication (Journal of Social Psychology, 755 cards) got 2% — recipients now read unsolicited 'gifts' as suspicious or as marketing. Reciprocity is real for genuine, personal, unexpected favours and evaporates when the favour looks like a pitch.
findings.source: Regan 1971 — https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/0022103171900254 ; Strohmetz et al. 2002 — https://scholarship.sha.cornell.edu/articles/130/ ; Kunz & Woolcott 1976 vs Meier 2015 — https://www.discovermagazine.com/mind/only-2-of-people-will-return-a-christmas-card-from-a-stranger
findings.honestApplication: The Meier replication is the warning: a discount popup framed as a gift reads as spam. What the store gives that is genuinely free and personal: (1) the full text of all five blessings, pointed, with sources, readable before buying — that is real value; label the /blessings pages as such ('לקריאה חופשית, גם בלי לקנות') rather than as a sales page. (2) The included card and padded box — already stated as 'כלולים בכל הזמנה'; keep that truthful (lib/extras.ts insists the paid box is an upgrade, not a replacement). (3) WhatsApp help that actually answers (support is the main channel) — a personal, non-automated reply is the modern equivalent of Strohmetz's 'manner of giving'. (4) A printable one-page PDF of the chosen blessing, or a short 'how to say Eshet Chayil on Friday night' guide, given without an email gate. Do not do: 'free gift with purchase' unless a real item is added, 'we planted a tree', or a 'gift' that requires the email first — that is the 2% case.

findings.principle: Authority (legitimate source and credentials)
findings.what: Bickman (1974, J. Applied Social Psychology 4:47–61, two field experiments): pedestrians asked to give a stranger a dime for a parking meter complied 89% when the requester wore a guard's uniform, 57% for a milkman, 33% for a civilian; for 'pick up this bag', 38% vs 14% vs 19%. Cialdini's authority principle rests on Milgram and on such uniform/credential studies; his often-cited physical-therapy example (patients complied 34% more after staff displayed diplomas) is a consulting anecdote reported in an ASU news piece, not a peer-reviewed study. The reliable core: visible, verifiable markers of legitimate expertise raise compliance; the marker must be checkable and relevant.
findings.source: Bickman 1974 — https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/j.1559-1816.1974.tb02599.x ; Cialdini physical-therapy example (practitioner) — https://news.wpcarey.asu.edu/20070131-gentle-science-persuasion-part-five-authority
findings.honestApplication: The store's authority is not the brand (it has none yet) but the source, and the site already uses it: chapter-and-verse references under every product name, the Westminster Leningrad Codex named as the text source, the sources line in the Hero. Extend only with checkable markers: (1) Name the engraving technology and, if the owner agrees, the fabrication partner or the specific instrument class — a named process beats 'advanced technology'. (2) Replace any synthesised chip visual with a real microscope photograph of a real chip from the store's own batch; a real image with a scale bar is authority, a rendered one is the opposite when discovered. (3) components/home/Process.tsx says every item ships with a serial number and certificate — that is an authority claim; verify it is operationally true for every order before it stays on the page. (4) If a rabbi or scholar actually proofread the texts, say who; if not, do not imply it. (5) The letter-height number should come from a measurement (CLAUDE.md open item 2) — a number with a method behind it is the store's most credible authority signal. Not allowed: 'as seen in', invented awards, or 'rabbinically approved' without a named approver.

findings.principle: Cart abandonment baseline and the ranked reasons (Baymard's 50-study meta figure + 2025 survey)
findings.what: Average documented cart abandonment rate is 70.22% (aggregate of 50 studies, last updated 22 Sep 2025). Ranked reasons for abandoning DURING checkout (2025 survey, 1,026 US respondents, 'just browsing' excluded): 40% extra costs too high (shipping/fees), 20% delivery too slow, 19% didn't trust the site with credit-card info, 18% site required an account, 17% checkout too long/complicated, 17% site errors/crashes, 13% returns policy unsatisfactory, 12% couldn't see total cost upfront, 10% card declined, 9% not enough payment methods. Baymard states a 35.26% conversion-rate increase is achievable 'through better checkout design' and that the average site has 39 checkout improvement areas.
findings.source: Baymard Institute, 'Cart Abandonment Rate Statistics' — https://baymard.com/lists/cart-abandonment-rate
findings.honestApplication: This is the priority map for mikra.shop. Already right: no account creation exists at all (removes the 18% reason), single-page checkout with 7 text fields (17% reason), server-side recomputed totals with full total in the button label (12% reason). What's still open, in this order: (1) the 40% 'extra costs' reason — the ₪29 shipping and ₪550 free-shipping threshold are not shown on the product page buy box (see next finding); (2) the 19% 'trust with card' reason — the checkout never names the processor or shows which real payment methods exist (see the perceived-security finding); (3) the 9% 'payment methods' reason is solved the day Grow goes live with cards/Bit/Apple Pay/Google Pay/PayPal. None of these levers require invented numbers; every figure needed already lives in lib/policy.ts.

findings.principle: Show estimated shipping cost on the product page (Baymard PDP study)
findings.what: 64% of users looked for shipping costs on the product page before adding to cart; 43% of e-commerce sites do not show any shipping cost or estimator on the product page; 21% of US shoppers abandoned because they 'weren't able to see the total order cost upfront before initiating the checkout'. Recommended first option: 'display the lowest flat-rate shipping cost available'. (Published 20 Jun 2017; abandonment figure from the 2025 survey.)
findings.source: Baymard Institute, 'Product Pages Need to Show Estimated Shipping Costs (Yet 43% of Sites Don't)' — https://baymard.com/blog/show-shipping-costs-on-product-pages
findings.honestApplication: Verified on the live page (curl of https://mikra.shop/products/toldot): '₪29' appears only inside the FAQ accordion near the bottom ('דמי המשלוח ₪29'), and '₪550' does not appear on the product page at all — the threshold surfaces only in the cart drawer progress bar. In components/ProductView.tsx, `shippingNote` is imported (line 29) but never rendered. Honest fix: one line under <DeliveryEstimate /> (line 579), sourced from lib/policy.ts: 'משלוח מבוטח ₪29 · חינם מעל ₪550 · או איסוף עצמי במודיעין ללא עלות'. Flat rate is real, threshold is real, pickup is real.

findings.principle: 'Free shipping' must not live only in a site-wide banner (banner blindness)
findings.what: 32% of sites display 'Free Shipping' only via banners/site-wide headers; in testing 'as many as 27% of users missed it' even while exploring product pages carefully. Free-shipping information 'should be placed near, but not in, the Buy section'. (Published 22 Aug 2017; 64% of users start considering shipping cost at the product-page stage.)
findings.source: Baymard Institute, 'Product Pages: Free Shipping Should Not Only Be in a Site-Wide Banner (32% Get It Wrong)' — https://baymard.com/blog/avoid-banners-only-free-shipping
findings.honestApplication: mikra.shop's PromoBar ticker (components/PromoBar.tsx) carries 'משלוח מבוטח · 2-4 ימי עסקים' but not the ₪550 threshold, and the threshold itself is only in CartDrawer.tsx (lines 237-259). That is exactly the banner-only pattern. The fix is the same single line under the buy button as above; it also makes the cart's 'עוד ₪X למשלוח חינם' bar the second exposure instead of the first. Note for the gift buyer: 11 of 15 models are ₪279-349, so the threshold is a real second-item nudge (documented in lib/policy.ts) — no invented scarcity needed.

findings.principle: Show a delivery DATE, not a delivery speed ('2-4 business days')
findings.what: 41% of sites (2023 article) / 48% (2025 benchmark) fail to show an estimated delivery date in the shipping-selection interface. When shown only speed, test participants 'came to a complete halt' trying to extrapolate the date, opened calendars, and reached different conclusions from identical information; ranges wider than 5-7 days caused hesitation, 'particularly for gift orders'. Phrasings like 'Arrives April 3rd–April 9th' all performed fine. (Published 27 Jun 2023; 2025 figure from the checkout benchmark.)
findings.source: Baymard Institute, 'Use Delivery Date Not Shipping Speed (41% Don't)' — https://baymard.com/blog/shipping-speed-vs-delivery-date ; benchmark figure at https://baymard.com/blog/current-state-of-checkout-ux
findings.honestApplication: Already right on the product page: components/DeliveryEstimate.tsx computes a real date window from POLICY.deliveryMinDays/MaxDays skipping Fri/Sat and renders 'מגיע אליכם 18-22 בספטמבר'. Missing in the checkout: the shipping radio (CheckoutForm.tsx lines 195-231) shows only `m.note` = 'מבוטח · 2-4 ימי עסקים' — the exact place Baymard measures. Fix: reuse addBusinessDays() in the delivery option note ('מגיע 18-22 בספטמבר') and for pickup 'בתיאום בוואטסאפ, כבר מחר'. One caution under the store's 'every number derivable' rule: lib/faq.ts line 43 says the parcel 'יוצאת תוך יום עסקים' AND arrives in 2-4 business days, while DeliveryEstimate counts 2-4 from now — decide whether the 2-4 window includes dispatch, otherwise the date is a day optimistic.

findings.principle: Guest checkout by default; save account creation for the confirmation page
findings.what: 18% of respondents abandoned because the site required an account (2025 survey); 62% of sites fail to make 'Guest Checkout' the most prominent option (2025 benchmark); 42% interrupt users before or during checkout to suggest account creation; Baymard's recommendation is to offer account creation only on the order-confirmation step. (Delayed-account article published 19 Sep 2023.)
findings.source: Baymard Institute, 'Save Account Creation for the Confirmation Step (42% Don't)' — https://baymard.com/blog/delayed-account-creation ; 2025 figures at https://baymard.com/blog/current-state-of-checkout-ux
findings.honestApplication: Already right: mikra.shop has no accounts, no login, no password — CheckoutForm goes straight to fields. The marketing checkbox is unticked and separate from the terms checkbox (lib/checkout.ts documents the Section 30א reasoning). Keep it that way; if a customer area is ever added, the only Baymard-sanctioned place for the offer is app/checkout/success after the order exists.

findings.principle: Minimise checkout form fields
findings.what: The average US checkout had 11.3 form fields in 2024 (down from 11.8 in 2021 and 12.7 in 2019), while 'most sites need only 8 form fields in total'; 17% of users have abandoned due to checkout complexity. Older figure: 'an ideal checkout flow can be as short as 12-14 form elements' vs. an average of 23.48 elements.
findings.source: Baymard Institute, 'Checkout Optimization: Minimize Form Fields' — https://baymard.com/blog/checkout-flow-average-form-fields ; element count at https://baymard.com/lists/cart-abandonment-rate
findings.honestApplication: Already right and slightly better than Baymard's ideal: lib/checkout.ts FIELDS = 7 text fields for delivery (first name, last name, email, phone, street, city, optional postcode) and 4 for pickup — address fields are removed when pickup is chosen (CheckoutForm.tsx line 253-255), there is no country selector (Israel only), no address-line-2, no company, no 'notes'. The gift-recipient block adds 5 fields only when the checkbox is ticked. Guard this: do not add a 'הערות' or 'שם על הכרטיס' field to the form; the FAQ already routes such things to WhatsApp.

findings.principle: Explain WHY the phone number (and email) is required
findings.what: 39% of e-commerce sites require a phone number without explanation (2025 benchmark; 49% 'don't explain why a phone number is required' in the 2025 checkout benchmark list); 14% of online shoppers 'refuse to provide their phone number to any online store'. In testing users asked 'why do they need my phone number? They don't need it!' and some entered fake data or abandoned; an explanation such as 'in case of delivery questions' (Everlane) or 'Only used to contact you in case of problems with your order or delivery' resolved it. 61% of the top 100 US sites required seemingly unnecessary info without explanation (2012 benchmark).
findings.source: Baymard Institute, 'Explain Why the Phone Field Is Required' — https://baymard.com/blog/explain-phone-number-field ; and 'Don't Require Seemingly Unnecessary Information (61% Get it Wrong)' — https://baymard.com/blog/checkout-experience-seemingly-unnecessary-information
findings.honestApplication: Missing: in lib/checkout.ts FIELDS, 'טלפון' and 'דוא״ל' are required with no reason shown; the only explanation that exists is buried in the validation error for the recipient phone ('טלפון הנמען, למשלוח'). Both reasons are literally true at mikra.shop, so the fix is a sub-label from the same source of truth: phone → 'לעדכוני השליח, ולקישור התשלום בוואטסאפ' (the manual flow in app/api/checkout/route.ts really sends the link by WhatsApp; the courier really calls); email → 'לאישור ההזמנה ולחשבונית'. Recipient phone → 'השליח מתקשר לנמען לפני המסירה' (this is why validate() makes it mandatory).

findings.principle: Mark BOTH required and optional fields explicitly
findings.what: Only 14% of sites explicitly mark both required and optional fields (2021 benchmark; 6% on mobile); 37% mark only optional fields, 42% only required. When only optional fields are marked, 32% of test users hit validation errors from incomplete required fields ('Is it something that I have to make up, or…?'). 2025 benchmark: 61% 'don't mark both required and optional fields explicitly'. Recommendation: asterisk for required + '(optional)' text next to the label for optional.
findings.source: Baymard Institute, 'E-Commerce Checkouts Need to Mark Both Required Fields and Optional Fields Explicitly (Only 14% Do So)' — https://baymard.com/blog/required-optional-form-fields
findings.honestApplication: Half right: CheckoutForm.tsx line 82 appends '(לא חובה)' to optional fields (postcode, recipient postcode), but required fields carry no marker. Fix is cosmetic: add an asterisk (or the word 'חובה') on required labels plus a one-line legend under the h1 — no new fields, no copy claims.

findings.principle: Inline validation done right + adaptive (specific) error messages
findings.what: 32% of sites 'fail to provide any field validation at all' (2024). Three rules: don't validate prematurely (before the user has typed), remove the error the moment the input is corrected, and use positive validation (check mark) which gave participants 'a sense of accomplishment and progression'. Separately, 94% of sites 'don't use adaptive error messages matching specific user issues' (2025 benchmark) and 86% show generic 'Invalid [field]' text; specific messages 'dramatically reduced the number of participants who got completely stuck'. (Inline-validation article published 9 Jan 2024.)
findings.source: Baymard Institute, 'Usability Testing of Inline Form Validation' — https://baymard.com/blog/inline-form-validation ; 'How to Improve Validation Errors' — https://baymard.com/blog/adaptive-validation-error-messages ; 2025 figure at https://baymard.com/blog/current-state-of-checkout-ux
findings.honestApplication: Mostly right: CheckoutForm.tsx validates only after the first submit attempt (`tried`), then re-validates on every keystroke so errors vanish as soon as they are fixed (line 71), focuses the first invalid field (line 119-120), and uses aria-invalid/aria-describedby. Some messages are already adaptive ('מיקוד בן 5 או 7 ספרות', the used-coupon message in route.ts). Missing: (a) no positive validation — a small check mark on fields that pass after the first attempt costs nothing; (b) phone/email messages are generic ('מספר טלפון ישראלי לא תקין') — validate() in lib/checkout.ts can say what it actually checks: '10 ספרות שמתחילות ב-05, אפשר גם +972' / 'חסר @ או סיומת'. All derived from the regexes already in the file.

findings.principle: Purpose-built touch keyboards on mobile (input type / inputmode)
findings.what: Across 48 major mobile sites, support for purpose-built keyboards rose only from 40% (2013) to 46% (2015); 54% fail to invoke optimised keyboards for phone, ZIP or card fields; 60% of top-50 mobile sites 'fail to utilize 2 of 5 keyboard optimizations'; auto-correction is neglected by 79% and auto-capitalisation by 27%. Baymard also warns type=number can strip leading zeroes on some browsers. Labels must sit above the field, and inline (placeholder-only) labels must be avoided.
findings.source: Baymard Institute, 'Touch Keyboard Implementations Have Improved Just 9% Since 2013 (60% Still Get it Wrong)' — https://baymard.com/blog/mobile-touch-keyboards ; '6 Mobile Checkout Usability Considerations' — https://baymard.com/blog/mobile-checkout
findings.honestApplication: Right: email uses type=email, phone uses type=tel, every field has a visible label above it (no placeholder-only labels), inputs are 46px tall, autoComplete tokens are set on buyer fields and deliberately off on recipient fields (documented reason in lib/checkout.ts). Missing: 'מיקוד' and 'toPostcode' are type='text' with no inputMode — Israeli 7-digit codes can start with 0, so the correct fix is inputMode="numeric" (not type=number) on both postcode entries in FIELDS/RECIPIENT_FIELDS. Purely technical, no copy.

findings.principle: Promo-code field visibility ('coupon hunting') and Apply buttons
findings.what: 35% of sites with promo fields display them expanded by default; once users notice the field 'they will often feel like they are overpaying', leave the checkout to hunt for codes, and 'the chance of them not returning to complete the purchase increases significantly'. Recommendation: collapse coupon fields behind a link placed secondary to the step's primary purpose, and 'if discounts can be autoapplied, do it'. On Apply buttons: 22% of sites still require them for ordinary fields; they 'can make sense' for promo codes and gift cards. (Apply article updated 14 May 2025.)
findings.source: Baymard Institute, 'How to Display Promotional Fields' — https://baymard.com/guidelines/615-how-to-display-promotional-fields ; 'Checkout UX: Avoid Apply Buttons' — https://baymard.com/blog/checkout-usability-apply-buttons

findings.principle: Perceived security of the payment step and trust seals (what users actually trust)

findings.principle: Verifiability of claims (Fogg guideline #1: 'Make it easy to verify the accuracy of the information on your site') — and the asymmetry that one broken claim erases all other trust work
findings.what: Stanford's Web Credibility guidelines (three years of research, 4,500+ people) put 'make it easy to verify accuracy' first: provide citations/source material and link to it, 'even if people don't follow these links, you've shown confidence in your material'. NN/g (Nielsen 1999, reaffirmed by Harley 2016 after new usability studies) states 'a single violation of trust can destroy years of slowly accumulated credibility'; in the 2016 studies a user abandoned a moving company after spotting one spelling error. Fogg et al. 2003 (2,684 participants evaluating live sites) found 'design look' dominated first impressions (46.1% of comments), with information structure and focus next.
findings.source: Stanford Persuasive Technology Lab, B.J. Fogg — https://credibility.stanford.edu/guidelines ; Fogg, Soohoo, Danielson et al. 2003, DUX '03 — https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/997078.997097 ; Nielsen Norman Group — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/communicating-trustworthiness/ and https://www.nngroup.com/articles/trustworthy-design/
findings.honestApplication: This is the store's own core promise ('אפשר לקרוא אותו כאן באתר לפני שקונים, ולהשוות למקור' in components/home/Assurance.tsx) and today it would fail its own test: per CLAUDE.md open decision #1, four of five blessings display text longer than the engraved file and the baby blessing shows a different text entirely; the '9 micron' letter height and three contradictory size numbers have no measurement behind them (open decision #2). Before adding ANY new trust signal: (a) decide the claims audit — either shorten the displayed text to the engraved file or re-engrave; (b) either measure the letter height or delete the number from Hero/craft SPECS/faq.ts; (c) make 'compare to source' literal: link each blessing page to an external canonical Tanakh text (e.g., Sefaria/mechon-mamre chapter URL) — that is Fogg #1 and NN/g factor 4 ('connected to the rest of the web') in one honest move, and it costs nothing.

findings.principle: 'A real organization behind the site' — physical address, registration number, phone (Fogg guidelines #2 and #5; trust antecedents in Bart et al. 2005 and Kim, Ferrin & Rao 2008)

Bart, Shankar, Sultan & Urban 2005 (6,831 consumers, 25 sites, 8 categories) found the drivers of online trust differ by category — privacy and order fulfillment dominate where information risk and involvement are high, and brand strength is critical in high-involvement categories; for a brand with no brand strength, the substitutes are the fulfillment and privacy signals. Kim, Ferrin & Rao 2008 (SEM on web-survey data) found trust and perceived risk strongly drive purchase, with company reputation, privacy/security concerns and information quality as antecedents.

findings.principle: Real people behind the site (Fogg guideline #4) — a named founder/maker with a real portrait beats any anonymous 'about'

Baymard seal surveys: 2013 (2,510 responses) Norton ~36% but 49% 'don't know/no preference'; 2022 (3,516 responses) Norton 35.4%, Google Trusted Store 20.9%, BBB 15.7%, McAfee 12.8%. findings.honestApplication: CLAUDE.md records 'אין דוא"ל יוצא' and 'אין התראה על הזמנה חדשה' while the success page promises a WhatsApp payment link 'בדרך כלל תוך שעה'. For a first-time buyer of an unknown brand, silence after paying is the moment trust collapses. Before scaling ads: (1) send a real order-confirmation email/WhatsApp with order number, chosen blessing, the delivery-date window and the phone number; (2) an internal new-order alert so the one-hour promise is kept; (3) put a 3-step 'מה קורה אחרי ההזמנה' (confirmation → engraving/verification → insured shipment with tracking) on the PDP or cart, using only steps that really happen. findings.principle: Warranty as a quality signal — works only when the warrantor is credible; a generous warranty from a doubted seller backfires (Boulding & Kirmani 1993)
findings.what: Boulding & Kirmani 1993 (JCR 20(1), experimental test of signaling theory) found consumers read warranties as quality signals only when the firm has credibility ('bonding'); 'if consumers question the willingness of the manufacturer to honor warranty obligations, then the offering of more extensive warranties will hinder rather than help product quality perceptions'.
findings.source: Boulding & Kirmani, Journal of Consumer Research 20(1), 1993 — https://academic.oup.com/jcr/article-abstract/20/1/111/1902098

findings.principle: Return-policy leniency: money and effort leniency raise purchases; a longer time window paradoxically lowers returns (Janakiraman, Syrdal & Freling 2016 meta-analysis)
findings.what: Meta-analytic review of 21 papers (Journal of Retailing 92(2), 2016): overall leniency increases purchases more than returns; monetary leniency (full refund) and low-effort leniency (easy process) are the dimensions that increase purchases; leniency in time reduces return rates (endowment effect); scope leniency (letting sale items be returned) also encourages buying. Baymard: 13% abandon for an 'unsatisfactory returns policy'.
findings.source: Janakiraman, Syrdal & Freling 2016 — https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0022435915000822 ; summary https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2016/01/160119141921.htm ; https://baymard.com/lists/cart-abandonment-rate

findings.principle: The handmade effect — products described as made by hand are seen as 'containing love' and are preferred especially when buying a gift for someone close (Fuchs, Schreier & Van Osselaer 2015)
findings.what: Four experiments (Journal of Marketing 79(2), 2015, pp. 98–110): stating handmade vs. machine-made production raised product attractiveness, driven by the belief that the maker's love is transferred into the object; consumers were willing to pay up to 17% more for handmade in general; participants asked to buy 'a gift for someone with whom they had a close relationship' clearly favored handmade items; the effect held even when the buyer did not know who the maker was.
findings.source: https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1509/jm.14.0018 ; summary https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2015/03/150324111544.htm

findings.principle: Show a delivery date, not a shipping speed — users read a stated date as a promise (Baymard, 2023)
findings.what: Baymard's large-scale checkout testing (article 27 June 2023): 41% of e-commerce sites show only shipping speed; with speed alone test participants 'come to a complete halt', opening calendars and reaching conflicting conclusions; participants treated a stated delivery date 'as a clear promise or guarantee of delivery by that date'; recommendation is to show the date in the shipping selector and on the product page when possible.
findings.source: https://baymard.com/blog/shipping-speed-vs-delivery-date

For gift buyers the date directly answers 'will it arrive before the birthday/ceremony' — pair it with the pickup-in-Modi'in alternative for last-minute gifts.

findings.what: NN/g (Nielsen 1999): 'reveal shipping charges immediately rather than waiting until after the user has placed an order'; Harley 2016: hidden costs and gated content damage trust. Baymard's abandonment reasons (non-browsing segment): 40% extra costs too high (shipping/tax/fees), 12% couldn't see or calculate total order cost up front, 9% insufficient payment methods.
